title: Halloween II
tagline: Same night, same town, second helping.
about: Picking up the same Halloween night in 1978, Laurie Strode is taken to Haddonfield Memorial Hospital while Dr Loomis hunts the streets for the masked man who attacked her.
cue: Serve the pumpkin seeds when the ambulance brings Laurie in.
faces: Serve the pumpkin seeds when the ambulance brings Laurie in.
Night shift eats at midnight, Halloween or not. Keep the corridor lights on and the doors locked.
Chicken, carrot, celery and peas in a creamy thyme sauce under a puff pastry lid
the security guard's supper at the front desk
Pepitas roasted with butter, brown sugar, smoked paprika and cinnamon until crunchy
Soft white bread with creamy egg, mayonnaise, mustard and chives, crusts off

Cloudy apple juice mulled with cinnamon, cloves, star anise, ginger and orange
Lunch is served at the usual time. Prices subject to change. Form CF-1978. 1981.

Haddonfield Memorial Hospital CafeteriaHalloween IISame night, same town, second helping.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersJack-o'-lantern pumpkin seedsPepitas roasted with butter, brown sugar, smoked paprika and cinnamon until crunchyHow to make it200g pepitas20g butter, melted1 tbsp brown sugar1 tsp smoked paprika1/2 tsp ground cinnamon1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1/2 tsp saltHeat the oven to 170°C. Toss the pepitas with the butter, sugar, paprika, cinnamon, cayenne and salt.Spread on a lined tray and roast, stirring halfway, until puffed and crunchy.Cool on the tray.Night shift egg sandwichesSoft white bread with creamy egg, mayonnaise, mustard and chives, crusts offHow to make it6 eggs4 tbsp mayonnaise1 tsp yellow mustard2 tbsp chives, snipped1/2 tsp salt1/4 tsp white pepper8 slices of soft white bread30g butter, softenedLower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes.Cool the eggs in iced water.Peel and mash with the mayonnaise, mustard, chives, salt and pepper.Butter the bread, fill, cut off the crusts and cut into fingers.MainsNight shift chicken pot pieChicken, carrot, celery and peas in a creamy thyme sauce under a puff pastry lidHow to make it800g chicken thigh fillets, in 3cm pieces40g butter1 onion, diced2 carrots, diced2 celery sticks, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed40g plain flour500ml chicken stock125ml thickened cream1 tsp thyme leaves1 cup frozen peas1 tsp salt1/2 tsp black pepper2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beatenBrown the chicken in half the butter and set aside.Soften the onion, carrots, celery and garlic in the rest of the butter.Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock and cream with the thyme and simmer until thick.Return the chicken with the peas, season with salt and pepper and cool a little while the oven heats to 200°C.Pour into a 2 litre pie dish, top with the pastry, crimp, cut a slit and brush with egg.Bake until puffed and deep golden.Rest before serving.Mr Garrett's meatball subsThe security guard's supper at the front deskHow to make it300g beef mince300g pork mince60g breadcrumbs1 egg30g parmesan, grated3 garlic cloves2 tbsp olive oil700ml passata1 tsp dried oregano4 long crusty rolls8 slices of provolone1 basil100g rocketMix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, 1 crushed garlic clove and salt, and roll into 20 meatballs.Brown the meatballs in the oil and lift out.Fry the rest of the garlic for 1 minute, add the passata and oregano, put the meatballs back and simmer for 20 minutes.Split and toast the rolls, fill with meatballs and sauce, lay over the provolone and grill for 2 minutes until melted.Tuck in the basil and serve with the rocket on the side.SweetsHaddonfield candy applesCrisp red apples dipped in glassy cinnamon red toffeeHow to make it6 small crisp red apples6 wooden sticks1 tsp vegetable oil, for the paper400g white sugar125ml water3 tbsp glucose syrup1 cinnamon stick1/2 tsp red food colouringWash the apples in hot water to strip the wax, dry well and push a stick into each. Oil a sheet of baking paper.Heat the sugar, water, glucose and cinnamon stick, stirring until dissolved, then boil without stirring to 150°C.Take off the heat, lift out the cinnamon and stir in the colouring.Tilt the pan and dip each apple, twirling to coat, then stand on the paper.Leave to set hard.DrinksNight shift mulled apple juiceCloudy apple juice mulled with cinnamon, cloves, star anise, ginger and orangeHow to make it1.5 L cloudy apple juice1 orange, sliced2 cinnamon sticks6 whole cloves2 star anises1 3cm piece ginger, sliced1 tbsp brown sugarPut everything in a pot and bring to just below a simmer.Keep on the lowest heat to infuse, without boiling.Strain into mugs and garnish with orange and cinnamon.
